paragraphs: The M3 Competition has been part of the M3 range since the F80 generation, and across its two generations has used two different engines — from the S55 through to today's S58. The F80-generation car (2014–2018) uses the S55, a 3.0-litre twin-turbo inline-six derived from the N55 but heavily reworked for M duty. From 2021, the G80-generation car switched to the S58 — a newer engine that's a genuine reliability improvement over the S55, with a closed-deck block and a redesigned crank hub arrangement. The full breakdown by engine code is below.
about.boldParagraph: The M3 Competition is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre twin-turbo inline-six fitted to the M3 Competition from 2014 to 2018 (F80 generation). Known for crank hub slip under hard use — we install a preventative crank hub upgrade as standard on every S55 rebuild, along with timing chain components, bearings and gaskets.
cards.cta: Check Your S55 BMW M3 Competition

cards.body: The current 3.0-litre twin-turbo inline-six, fitted from 2021. A genuine reliability improvement over the S55 — closed-deck block, fixed the rod bearing issue, well-proven B58 architecture. No significant defect pattern confirmed.

compatibility.intro: Because the M3 Competition spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an S55 part will work on an S58 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic M3 Competition quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
